votes.reason: NVDA is the purest way to hold my lead Technology call: it is the AI-chain chipmaker that led tech's best week of 2026 (+11.6% against XLK's +7.2% and SMH's +7.8%), the Aug 26 report my thesis counts on is still ahead, and the hot-CPI risk I flagged hits the whole sector, not this name in particular.

My Industrials call is built on CAT, because its record Q2 on AI data-center power demand is my evidence alongside ISM at 55.6 and XLI's new 52-week high, and it bounced 3.4% last week; the only caveat is that Industrials is my lowest-conviction call, so 25% is the most I would give it.

GOOGL fits my Technology call, whose thesis cites Alphabet's +82% cloud growth as support for the AI chain; it slipped 0.5% while XLK rose 7.2%, so it is riding the AI business rather than last week's rate-relief rally, which is a caution about momentum rather than a sector reason to object.

PGR is in Financials, the one sector I weighed and turned down this week, and the draft gives it the job of cushioning a hot CPI, which I judged Financials can't do and gave to Healthcare instead (XLF lagged SPY by 2.35% in last week's rally against XLV's 1.59%), so it works against my calls rather than expressing one and leaves my hedge sector with no name in the book.

FCX fits my Materials call squarely as a copper producer in the only sector beating SPY over both the week and the month, with the dollar near 99.6; it has run hard (+11.2% on the week) but it is not the stretched gold name I flagged (NEM), and the 10% size matches my risk of the dollar turning back up.
